0.1.6.title: Imported tracks come back into view
0.1.6.summary: Tracks imported from a playlist are stored at their real path, so the folder that owns them can find them again.
highlights: Tracks imported from a playlist in a sibling folder were stored at a path no watched folder could match, so they never appeared and were never analysed. Existing libraries are repaired on launch.
The track list says why a track needs attention — not analysed, ambiguous key, low key confidence or clipping — and carries the key and tempo confidence.
Crates keep a playing order you can read, reorder and export as an .m3u8 playlist.
Watched folders can be added, removed and rescanned without opening the window.

0.1.5.title: Silence leaves a record, and an interface you can size
0.1.5.summary: When a track fails to play or takes too long to start, the steps that led there are written down. The whole interface can also be scaled to the display you are on.
highlights: Interface scale: Cmd / Ctrl with + and − size the whole window, not just the text. Cmd / Ctrl 0 goes back to 100%, and the size is remembered per display.
A track that fails, or takes too long to start, now writes the steps that led there to a log file — Settings › About › Show log file.
Show log file says when nothing has been recorded yet, instead of looking like a broken button on a healthy install.
The virtual piano reads as a surface again against the lighter window.
The dark theme's surfaces were lifted off near-black, and now match Capstone and Stack rung for rung.

0.1.4.title: Your folders, your cue counts, and markers you can read
0.1.4.summary: A new Library pane for the folders Keystone watches, a way back when a file moves, and cue markers that no longer print on top of each other.
highlights: Settings now has a Library pane: see the folders Keystone watches, re-scan one after adding files outside the app, and remove one you no longer want.
When a track's file moves or its drive is unplugged, Check for missing files finds it. Nothing is deleted — cleaning up is a separate, clearly-marked step.
Cue markers that sit close together stack onto separate rows instead of printing over each other.
The CUES column shows how many cue points each track has, instead of a dash on every row.
Play counts are counted.

0.1.3.title: Drag that lands, tempo you can correct, and in-app updates
0.1.3.summary: Dropping a track onto a collection now goes where you point it, the BPM is editable by hand, and Keystone can finally update itself.
highlights: Dragging tracks to a collection lands on the row you are pointing at, and shows the key, energy and tempo of what you are carrying while you drag.
Correct a BPM by hand, with halve and double for tracks read at the wrong octave. It survives re-analysis, like the key and energy overrides.
In-app updates work. Version 0.1.0 could not check for them at all, so this one has to be installed by hand — after that Keystone updates itself.
Filing a batch of tracks no longer fails outright when one of them has been removed from the library since you listed it.
Fixed a 'database is locked' error that could make filing tracks fail while a scan was running.
Keystone's library can now be read and edited by an AI assistant that speaks MCP: search, overrides, collections, tags, renaming and export.

0.1.0.title: First release
0.1.0.summary: Keystone reads your track library, shows key, tempo and energy on a Camelot wheel, and writes what it finds back to your files.
highlights: Camelot wheel: pick a key and the library narrows to it and to everything that mixes with it.
Key, tempo and energy on every row, with cue markers you drag on the waveform.
Where a key is genuinely ambiguous, Keystone shows both candidates instead of guessing a letter.
Write key, energy and tempo into your tags or your filenames, with a preview first and an undo after.
Send cue points to rekordbox and Traktor. Your collection is backed up before anything is written.
Collections, ratings, bulk tag editing and search across the whole library.
Import playlists from the Music app, or from any .m3u.
Everything runs on your machine. No account, no uploads.
